analysis.title: October Jobs Preview (US Macro Snapshot)
key_insights: Natixis forecasts October nonfarm payrolls at +55k (prior 29k), slightly below the 60k consensus estimate.
Job gains have been volatile month to month, but the prevailing view of the labor market is stability. Initial jobless claims are low and payroll gains have averaged about 68k this year.
A payroll print in line with the Natixis forecast would not change the narrative of a solid but unspectacular labor market.
The unemployment rate is expected to rise slightly in October but stay at 4.2% on a rounded basis, helped by higher participation from prime-age workers.
Natixis expects upward pressure on the unemployment rate in coming months as hiring slows, personal savings dwindle and labor force participation rises.

The low-hire, low-fire dynamic has limited labor churn and kept wage pressures subdued. Average hourly earnings should rebound in October from a weak September print, but wage gains are likely to add little inflationary pressure.
The Fed's concern remains inflation. Natixis expects the story to stay the same after Friday's jobs print, with focus shifting to next week's CPI.
Over the last 10 years, September payrolls have been revised down three times.
